info.title: sliderule-cli
info.description: SlideRule is a .NET architecture checker that enforces one C# spec and renders the same rules for coding agents. A rule is either the law (Enforce) or a ratchet over a counted baseline (Migrate). A scope either fails a new reference into it (Quarantine) or only warns when a change touches it (Caution). The tool checks a solution at the command line, in CI and when a coding agent's turn ends. Agents read the rules in a managed AGENTS.md block and per-directory rule cards, and query them over MCP with 'sliderule mcp'. It is built for long-lived, business-critical .NET codebases.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Evaluate rules against a target solution; a project that fails to load, or whose NuGet packages did not resolve, fails the run (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the machine-readable JSON document instead of human-readable output. [default: False]

options.name: --diff-base
options.description: A git ref; files changed since it are checked against quarantined and cautioned scopes (the scope tripwire) — warnings only, never failures.

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Check against the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of failing the run with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --sarif
options.description: Write a SARIF 2.1.0 report to <path> (GitHub code scanning et al.); human/--json output is unchanged.

options.name: --rules
options.description: Check only the rules whose ID matches these globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed and it spans '/'); the report, the summary counts and the 0/1 verdict then cover that subset alone. A filter matching no rule refuses the run (exit 2) and lists the available rule IDs.

options.name: --grain
options.description: How much of the --json report to keep, each rung coarser than the one before it and never narrower: full (the default); overview, every rule and violation with each violation's sites replaced by their count; skeleton, every rule with its prose, status, baseline and warnings and its violations replaced by their count; index, a verdict per rule ID with the prose, the NuGet audit advisories and the workspace diagnostics elided (packageAuditCount and workspaceDiagnosticCount say how many) and every trust stamp kept, which is the menu --rules globs pick from.

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

options.name: --binlog
options.description: A .binlog from a real build of this solution on this machine. Replays the captured structure instead of a design-time build; the capture persists, and later runs replay it automatically while structurally valid.

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Print a rule's because, fix, citation, exemplar, posture payload, and linked prose; or, with --type or --path, which layers, rules and scopes claim a type, and why.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

options.name: --type
options.description: Explain a type instead of a rule: which layers, rules and scopes claim it, and why. A full name as check reports it, or a simple name.

options.name: --path
options.description: Explain every type a file or directory declares instead of a rule, absolute or relative to the solution.

arguments.name: RULE_ID
arguments.description: The rule ID to explain (a post-desugar ID, e.g. legacy/billing/containment). Omit it with --type or --path.

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: render
commands.description: Render the managed AGENTS.md block(s) from the spec, and sliderule.model.json where --model is passed or the file exists; a project that fails to load, or whose NuGet packages did not resolve, refuses the command (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Render from the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing the command with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --model
options.description: Write sliderule.model.json, the built model as data, beside the root AGENTS.md. Needed once: any later render refreshes a model file that exists. [default: False]

options.name: --diagram
options.description: Also render two Mermaid diagrams into <path>'s managed block: the codebase graph (projects and their cross-project references; solid = observed, dotted = declared but unobserved), then the spec's law (the places it names, what they must not reference, and the debt it grandfathers). The graph draws the projects the solution file declares, so a project a ProjectReference dragged into the build is not drawn; `graph` lists every loaded project and says which is which.

options.name: --diagram-only
options.description: Draw only the declared projects matching these name globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed) — for legibility on a large solution, not to keep a foreign project out. Scopes the codebase survey fence only, never the law fence. With --diagram.

options.name: --diagram-exclude
options.description: Drop the declared projects matching these name globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed) — for legibility on a large solution, not to keep a foreign project out. Scopes the codebase survey fence only, never the law fence. With --diagram.

options.name: --check
options.description: Write nothing: compare every file this render would write with the one on disk, name each that differs, and exit 1 if any does. For CI, in place of a render followed by git diff. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: baseline
commands.description: Grandfather, shrink, add one attributed exception to, or rename the ratcheted baselines. init, accept-reductions and add refuse (exit 2) when a project fails to load or its NuGet packages did not resolve, unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed; rename reads only the spec and the baseline files.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Grandfather each uncaptured ratcheted rule's current violations into its baseline. Always extracts fresh, because a rule it cannot see would be recorded as zero debt.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Write baselines from the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing the command with exit 2. [default: False]

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: accept-reductions
commands.description: Remove baseline entries whose violations no longer occur and lower recorded site counts; never adds. Always extracts fresh, because a violation it cannot see would be deleted as fixed.

options.name: --spec

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics

commands.name: add
commands.description: Grandfather exactly one currently observed violation of a captured rule, with attribution: an edge (--source with --target) or a shape (--subject).

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --rule
options.description: The ratcheted rule ID to add the entry to.

options.name: --because
options.description: Why this entry is grandfathered — recorded in the baseline entry (single line).

options.name: --source
options.description: The referencing type of the edge to grandfather — a full type name or 'T:' symbol ID.

options.name: --target
options.description: The referenced type of the edge to grandfather — a full type name or 'T:' symbol ID, or a banned member's full name (System.DateTime.Now) or member symbol ID (P:System.DateTime.Now).

options.name: --subject
options.description: The offending type of the shape violation to grandfather — a full type name or 'T:' symbol ID.

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Write baselines from the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing the command with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Move a renamed rule's baseline section from its old rule ID to its new one, with every entry kept and re-sealed. Reads the spec and the baseline files, never the code.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --from
options.description: The rule ID the baseline section is filed under: the rule's old ID, which the spec no longer declares.

options.name: --to
options.description: The rule's new ID: a ratcheted rule in the spec with no baseline section yet.

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the machine-readable JSON burndown document instead of human-readable output. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Report the burndown from the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of exiting 2 after rendering it. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

options.name: --binlog

commands.name: graph
commands.description: Summarize the codebase: projects, declared vs observed project references, namespace inventory, and grouped external references. Needs no spec; a project that fails to load or to restore refuses the survey (exit 2) unless --allow-workspace-diagnostics is passed.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the machine-readable JSON survey document instead of human-readable output. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-workspace-diagnostics
options.description: Survey the partial model even when some projects fail to load or to restore, instead of refusing with exit 2. [default: False]

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Bypass the persisted caches (extraction fragments and the build capture): always load and extract fresh, and write nothing back. [default: False]

options.name: --binlog
options.description: A .binlog from a real build of this solution on this machine. Replays the captured structure instead of a design-time build; the capture persists, and later runs replay it automatically while structurally valid.

options.name: --grain
options.description: How much of the survey to keep, each rung coarser than the one before it and never narrower: full (the default); overview, the whole survey with each project's namespace inventory elided; skeleton, the structural spine, every project with its frameworks, packaging facts, declared project references and type count and the observed project edges, with its package references elided and the external references, multiply declared types and shadowed types each reported as a count; index, the project roster, every project with its solution membership and type count alone and the observed edges, NuGet audit advisories and workspace diagnostics each reported as a count, which is the menu --projects globs pick from.

options.name: --projects
options.description: Survey only the projects matching these name globs (semicolon-separated, '*' allowed); references in both directions are kept, so an edge can name a project outside the scope. A filter matching no project refuses the survey (exit 2) and lists the available names.

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Run the MCP stdio server bound to a solution and spec.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution. Omit to use the convention.

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, a directory to search, or omitted to walk up from the working directory.

commands.name: hook
commands.description: Run as a Claude Code hook: read the event's payload on stdin, check the working tree when an agent's turn ends, and answer in Claude Code's exit codes. 0 lets the stop stand, with any tripwire warnings on stdout as context for the agent; 2 refuses it, with the report on stderr; 1 is SlideRule's own error, reported on stderr without blocking.

options.name: --spec
options.description: A built spec DLL, or a csproj that is a member of the target solution, relative to the working tree the hook fires for. Omit it to use the settings file, or the convention.

options.name: --diff-base
options.description: The git ref the check's scope tripwires read changed files from when no turn record stands: an edit, a hand run, or a stop with no state. A stop with one reads the files the turn changed. Warnings only, never failures. [default: HEAD]

options.name: --max-rounds
options.description: How many consecutive continuations one prompt may get from a red rule or a warning. Past it the hook reports the red rule without blocking, and the turn ends. [default: 3]

arguments.name: SOLUTION
arguments.description: Solution file, or a directory to search, relative to the working tree the hook fires for. Omit it to use the settings file, or the walk up from that tree.
